text:
Bitcoin successfully defended its $64,000 support floor before rallying to $65,300 late June 22, galvanized by a dramatic 87% deceleration in spot ETF outflows. This stabilization suggests institutional selling exhaustion, complemented by legacy giants aggressively deepening their digital footprints. Notably, ICE announced a transformative joint venture with OKX to launch a U.S.-regulated broker-dealer, while Franklin Templeton finalized its acquisition of 250 Digital to establish a dedicated "Franklin Crypto" division.

Simultaneously, the stablecoin ecosystem marked a maturity milestone as Bullish became the first centralized exchange to list SoFi Bank's regulated SoFiUSD, bridging traditional banking liquidity with crypto markets.

Despite these bullish microstructural developments, digital assets face fierce macro headwinds. Following hawkish repricing, the 2-year Treasury yield hit a 16-month high of 4.23% while the 10-year yield anchors near 4.50%. This restrictive curve, coupled with a dominant DXY near 101.0, forces crypto to absorb immense gravity from the risk-free rate to maintain parity with record-high equities.
